label: prop:plancherel-weight-boundedness
title: Plancherel weights define a probability distribution: $\sum_\lambda w_\lambda = 1$, $0 \leq w_\lambda \leq 1$
html:
Proposition. Plancherel weights define a probability distribution: \sum_\lambda w_\lambda = 1, 0 \leq w_\lambda \leq 1

For semisimple A = H_n(R, q), the canonical Plancherel weights w_\lambda(1) = (\dim V_\lambda)^2/n! fulfill strict probability-distribution conditions:

  1. Non-negativity: Each w_\lambda(1) \in [0, 1].
  2. Normalisation: \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} w_\lambda(1) = 1 exactly in \mathbb{Q}.

The classical dimension mapping guarantees standard conservation laws inside the algebra.
